A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ROC-n-reroll study. Their text, figures, equations and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved between sections.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix D report original GSM8K generator/verifier experiments and empirical RS and BoN scaling results.

after.justification: Section 6 and Appendix F report original per-question experiments and aggregate GSM8K and MATH500 evaluation results.

M1.justification: v2 Section 6 adds a verification variant that averages five scoring responses, alongside retained single-CoT verifiers. This changes the verification procedure modestly; the core RS acceptance and BoN selection rules remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds actual MATH500 evaluation alongside GSM8K (Section 6, Figure 5). v1's empirical evaluation is confined to GSM8K, so the second benchmark substantially broadens the evidence's dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Matched experiments retain RS versus BoN and the same Qwen3 and Llama verifier alternatives. The earlier four-verifier Qwen comparisons and two-verifier Llama comparisons remain in v2 Figure 4 and Appendix F. No new competing resampling method is evaluated.

E3.justification: The reported per-question generation pool changes from 10,000 responses in v1 to 1,000 in v2. New full-test-set evaluations cap RS at 25 attempts with an incorrect null fallback; MATH500 generation and verification also have 5,000-token limits. These are substantial revised and added evaluation protocols.

E4.justification: v2 adds GSM8K question 58 as another case study of similar early scaling followed by divergent performance. It also explicitly assesses theory–simulation discrepancies for the Llama example, reporting absolute errors below one percentage point (Section 6, Figure 4). Earlier synthetic ROC demonstrations and other question-level analyses remain.

E5.justification: v1 reports 95% bootstrap confidence intervals and specifies 1,000 bootstrap resamples for its empirical experiments. v2 removes the per-question intervals and bootstrap-count description, while its new aggregate Figure 5 reports exact 90% confidence intervals. This substantially changes uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds question-58 results and aggregate GSM8K/MATH500 accuracy curves, showing RS's early compute advantage and BoN approaching its performance later. Matched results also change, including the Llama question-7 curves (v1 Figure 9; v2 Figure F.5), and numerical AUROC annotations disappear. Changed reported settings preclude interpreting these as same-setting performance gains or losses.

T1.justification: v2 adds results and proofs connecting KL-regularized RL to RS, establishing RS dominance at matched expected compute, and showing BoN non-extrapolability (Propositions 4, 6 and 7). Proposition 3 gains stronger limiting-accuracy and concavity cases; Appendix C adds a mixture characterization of BoN scaling (Theorem 2). v1's hardness Remark 1 disappears. The compact BoN integral and discrete-score smoothing already existed in v1's appendices.

C1.justification: v1's explicit non-extrapolation claim concerns RS. v2 extends it to BoN and makes the impossibility of extrapolating either method a central abstract and introduction takeaway. The ROC characterization and shared asymptotic-accuracy claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds a qualified interpretation connecting verifier-limited RS accuracy to RL, distinguishes per-query guarantees from aggregate observations, and discusses distributional assumptions and budget-specific verifier training (Sections 4.4, 6–7). v1's generation-versus-verification hardness interpretation is removed; the main ROC-based explanations remain.

D1.justification: Appendices F–G add MATH500 answer parsing with math-verify and its boxed-answer prompt, disclose GSM8K exact-match checking, and explicitly state that Qwen3 thinking mode is unused. Existing GSM8K/verifier prompts and chat-encoding code are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds targeted references on verifier failures, calibration, MATH and RL, including Petrov et al., Bavaresco et al., Tian et al. and Rafailov et al.; the bootstrap reference disappears. Positioning relative to pass@N, imperfect-reward BoN and ROC analysis largely remains, with background moved to Appendix B.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and theoretical exposition are extensively rewritten. RS/BoN definitions are consolidated in Section 3.1, related-work background moves to Appendix B, corollaries become equations or inline statements, proofs are reorganized, and a Discussion section is added.

P2.justification: Empirical plots are substantially redrawn with changed axis ranges, legends, marker/line encodings and Llama panel order. v2 adds aggregate Figure 5, replaces the main Figure 1 example with question 58, relocates v1 Figure 4 to Figure F.3, and expands the notation table.

improvement.justification: v2 supplies a matched-compute dominance proof where v1 relied mainly on initial-slope comparisons and empirical examples, and tests key conclusions across full GSM8K and MATH500 datasets. These additions substantially strengthen the paper's formal foundation and empirical support. Removing per-question bootstrap intervals and resampling details is a reporting regression, but it does not outweigh those gains and the clearer organization.
